hypotheses.reasoning: The POST /v1/events 503s trace back to the third-party geo-IP provider (api.geoip.example). At 19:11:22 enrichment-svc first logs the provider returning HTTP 503 'Service Unavailable' (#3460); the gateway's first events 503 follows at #3462. The provider then degrades further: 502 responses (#3575) and 10s timeouts with no response (#3522, #3611). Enrichment's circuit breaker for the provider opens at 19:12:56 with a 96% failure rate (#3661). ingest-api then fails enrich calls fast with 'enrichment-svc returned 503 (circuit open)' (#3795), and the gateway returns 503 on POST /v1/events (#3612, #3756). Analytics 429 retries and drops are downstream noise. Before 19:11:22 the events path was healthy (#3431-#3443 all 200s), so the onset lines up with the provider failure. The provider's fast 503 points to external_outage; its later 10s hangs could also be read as dependency_timeout, which is why confidence is not higher.

A separate, concurrent fault breaks the login path. Migration 0094_add_status_v2 ran at 19:15:01. Step 1 renamed accounts.status_v2 to status_v2_old and committed; step 2 then failed with a lock timeout (#3989). The DDL is non-transactional, so the rename was not rolled back. From 19:16:14, account-svc queries for status_v2 fail with 'column does not exist' (#4089, #4155, #4186), and edge-proxy returns 500 on POST /login (#4141, #4192). This does not explain the POST /v1/events 503s, since the events path does not touch accounts-db. It is a real, separate integrity problem to triage on its own, and it starts after the events 503s began, so it is not their cause.

verdict.recommendedAction: Treat the geo-IP provider (api.geoip.example) as the origin of the POST /v1/events 503s. Confirm its status with the vendor and escalate. Mitigate on our side: serve geo lookups from geo-cache or a fallback, or let enrichment skip the geo step so events are accepted without it. Lower the 10s enrichment timeout so ingest-api threads are not held. The circuit breaker's half-open probes (#3877, #4756) should close it once the provider recovers. Separately, fix the login-path schema break: restore accounts.status_v2 (currently status_v2_old after the non-transactional rename in migration 0094) or complete the migration correctly, then verify /login recovers.

hypotheses.reasoning: The POST /v1/events 503s trace back to the third-party geo-IP provider (api.geoip.example). Enrichment's circuit breaker for the provider opens at 19:12:56 with a 96% failure rate (#3661). ingest-api then fails enrich calls fast with 'enrichment-svc returned 503 (circuit open)' (#3795, #4093), and the gateway returns 503 on POST /v1/events (#3612, #3756, #4102). Analytics 429 retries and drops are downstream noise. Before 19:11:22 the events path was healthy (e.g. #3431-#3443 all 200s), so the onset lines up with the provider failure. The provider's fast 503 response points to external_outage. Its later 10s hangs could also be read as dependency_timeout, which is why confidence is not higher.
hypotheses.recommendedAction: Treat the geo-IP provider as the origin. Confirm its status with the vendor and escalate. Mitigate on our side: keep the circuit breaker, serve geo lookups from geo-cache or a fallback, or let enrichment bypass the geo step so events are accepted without it. Reduce the 10s enrichment timeout so ingest-api threads are not held. Once the provider recovers, the half-open probe should close the circuit (watch the probes at #3877 and #4756). Do not roll back any deploy; none is implicated on this path.
